capability_summary: Supplies the company's authoritative brand definition - colour values and their roles, typography, logo variants and usage rules, and tone - to any downstream producer of an asset: generated imagery, UI code, print, or social. Emits a usable brand specification with each value attributed to its source, and surfaces contested values rather than resolving them silently.
user_goal: Produce or check an asset that is unmistakably on-brand, with brand values that are traceable to a stated source and safe to hand to a designer, developer, print vendor, or image generator.
success_looks_like: The asset or spec states exact hex values, typefaces and weights, not adjectives like 'warm orange' or 'modern sans'.
Every stated colour carries its source: a named design token, the logo artwork, an official theme declaration, or a documented print/social value.
Logo usage is specified concretely: which variant, clearspace, minimum size, and permitted backgrounds.
For image generation, the logo and wordmark are composited afterwards from an approved file, never described for the model to draw.
Where the brand's primary value is genuinely contested, the competing values are shown with their sources and the choice is escalated, not quietly made.
One asset uses one consistent value per brand role throughout.
Semantic roles the producer will need - accessible text variant, tint, shade, info, success, error - are supplied rather than left to invention.
A developer, printer or image model can act on the output without further interpretation.

priority_qualities.why_it_matters: A hex with no stated origin cannot be checked, and wrong brand colour is the most visible failure mode.
Silently picking a side manufactures false authority and propagates an unverified value into print and artwork.
Two different primaries in one deliverable is immediately visible and unambiguously wrong regardless of which value is correct.
Redrawn, distorted, or crowded marks are the fastest way an asset reads as counterfeit.
Web tokens, print, and generative imagery have different constraints; applying one blindly to another produces unusable output.
Missing semantic roles force the producer to invent off-brand values.
The output must be directly usable without the reader resolving ambiguity themselves.

constraints: Attribute every colour value to a source type: design token, logo artwork, official theme declaration, or documented print/social value.
Design tokens are authoritative for web UI. They are not automatically authoritative for the logo mark itself, nor for print, merchandise, or generated imagery that never consumed those tokens.
When a value is contested, present the competing values with their sources and let the requester decide; do not average, blend, or invent an intermediate.
Supply the full orange family - base, accessible-on-light text variant, tint and shade - not the base alone.
Supply the semantic roles including info blue alongside success and error.
Enumerate the logo variant set when logo usage is specified, and name which variant applies to the background in question.
State the clearspace rule and both minimum sizes (screen and print) whenever logo placement is specified.
Composite, don't generate: logos and wordmarks are overlaid from an approved asset file after image generation; the generator is instructed to reserve clear space for them.
State typefaces with their roles, weights and fallback stack.
When a brand decision falls outside the definition, derive it from the nearest documented rule and label the derivation as such rather than presenting it as established.
never_do: Never instruct an image generator to draw, render, or spell the logo, wordmark, or company name.
Never state a hex for the logo mark that differs from the artwork's actual colour.
Never attribute a value to a named design token unless that token resolves to it.
Never present a contested primary as settled fact.
Never use two different values for the same brand role within a single asset.
Never recolour, stretch, rotate, add effects to, or place the logo on a background that fails contrast.
Never substitute a near-miss colour or an unlisted typeface because an exact value was unavailable.
Never specify the base primary orange as the colour of small text on a light background.
objective_invariants: Every hex value in the output is accompanied by a stated source type.
Any value attributed to a named design token equals the value that token resolves to.
Any value stated as the logo mark's colour equals the artwork's colour.
No single asset or spec contains two different hex values assigned to the same brand role.
A contested brand value appears labelled as contested, with at least two competing values and their sources.
The orange family appears with base, accessible text variant, tint and shade values, not base alone.
The info blue appears as a named semantic role with a hex value.
The logo variant set is enumerated when logo usage is specified, and the applicable variant is named.
The clearspace rule and both minimum sizes appear whenever logo placement is specified.
Any image-generation prompt contains no instruction to render the logo, wordmark, or company name, and reserves space for post-generation compositing.
Typography is stated as role plus family plus weights plus fallback stack.
Divergence from a design-token value is permitted only for the logo mark, print, or non-token media, and only when the alternative source is named.
Any value not present in the brand definition is labelled as a derivation with the rule it was derived from.

competing_values.source: Production design token circleTel-orange in the web build configuration; several thousand usages across the shipped user interface
Explicitly labelled official theme colour declared in the application root layout; ships in production
The brand documentation's own stated primary value
Pixel sampling of the approved logo artwork files

contested_facts.note: The final three cluster within one unit per channel of each other; the design-token value sits materially further away. This may indicate a deliberate marketing-versus-interface split, or unintended drift. It is not resolved here.

competing_values.source: Production design token circleTel-navy; several hundred usages in the shipped interface
The brand documentation's stated secondary; the corresponding token has no usages and is marked legacy in the build configuration

competing_values.value: Manrope for display, Inter for body and interface, JetBrains Mono for code
competing_values.source: Fonts actually loaded by the application root layout
The brand documentation's stated typography; not loaded anywhere in production
Production design token, and the grey sampled from the logo artwork
The brand documentation's stated grey; corresponds to an interface muted-text colour rather than the mark

uncontested_facts: Accessible orange for text on light backgrounds: #AE5B16 (approximately 4.9:1 on white). Both candidate base oranges fail WCAG AA as text on white.
Eight approved logo variant files exist, covering full colour on light, full colour on dark, reversed, monochrome, and icon-only uses.
Clearspace: minimum clear space on all sides equal to the height of the 'TEL' element of the wordmark; no other element, text, or edge may enter it.
Minimum sizes: 32px on screen, 10mm in print.
The logo is composited from an approved file; it is never generated, redrawn, or spelled by a model.
scope_in: Colour palette with roles, hex values and source attribution
Typography families, roles, weights and fallback stacks
Logo variants, clearspace, minimum sizes and background rules
Brand tone and voice descriptors for copy within assets
Checking a produced asset against the brand definition
Supplying brand values to non-image consumers such as interface code, print and social
scope_out: Choosing or ratifying which contested value becomes canonical
Editing design token source files or logo artwork
Layout, grid, spacing, elevation and component design, which belong to the interface design system
Marketing strategy, campaign concepting and copywriting itself
General accessibility auditing beyond brand colour and logo-background contrast
scope_verdict: This is the authoritative brand definition; generated imagery is one consumer among several, alongside interface code, print and social. In scope when an asset in any medium needs authoritative brand values or a brand check. Out of scope when the request is to settle a contested value - that is escalated to the brand owner with the competing values and their sources presented.
activation_expectations: Activates when generating imagery, interface code, print or social assets that must carry the brand.
Activates when asked for brand colours, fonts, logo rules or tone.
Activates when reviewing an asset for brand correctness.
Activates when another producer is about to state a brand value, so the value can be sourced rather than recalled.
Does not activate for general design or layout work with no brand-value dependency.
Does not activate for interface system concerns such as spacing scales or component anatomy.
non_qualities: Length or verbosity of the output
Volume of rationale or justification prose
Naming internal file locations or implementation details
Producing an answer quickly at the cost of stating sources
Use of headings, tables or any particular document structure
